question_text: According to the course material, ACC203 Introduction to Financial Accounting I is a course material you are expected to study as a:
option_a: B.Sc. Accounting Student in National Open University of Nigeria
explanation: The course guide is for a B.Sc. Accounting student in NOUN.

question_text: According to the course material, accounting consists of designing and operating an efficient accounting information system for collection, recording, measuring, summarising, analysing and communicating the results of financial transactions for a particular period to users so they can:
explanation: Accounting communicates results to users for informed decisions.

question_text: According to the course material, accounting is usually referred to as the language of business; it has its own rules, for example debit the receiver, credit the giver, and symbols such as:
explanation: Rules include debit the receiver, credit the giver; symbols include Dr, Cr.

question_text: According to the course material, the professional accounting bodies in Nigeria, in addition to other recognised international bodies, are the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria (ICAN) and:
option_a: Association of National Accountants of Nigeria (ANAN)
explanation: Nigerian professional bodies named: ICAN and ANAN.

question_text: According to the course material, accounting is a science because it follows a systematic and organised body of knowledge; one of the accounting principles is the double entry system, which means that all accounting transactions have two parts to them, that is:
explanation: Double entry: every transaction has debit and credit.

question_text: According to the course material, qualities of good accounting information include relevance, objectivity, completeness, timeliness, comparable, clarity, accuracy and flexibility; good accounting information should be relevant to:
option_a: the purpose for which it is prepared
explanation: Relevance: enough facts and figures to satisfy the need of the users.

question_text: According to the course material, objectivity requires that accounting information should be free from thoughts and feelings of the person preparing the report, and that bias and window dressing should not be introduced; ability to trace all accounting transactions to:
explanation: Objectivity: trace transactions to source documents; no bias or window dressing.

question_text: According to the course material, the entity concept sees an organisation as a legal entity, separate and distinct from its owners; business records are kept separately from the owners even where the business is owned by:
explanation: Even a one-person business is recorded separately from the owner.

question_text: According to the course material, the going concern concept states that when recording the account of a business it should be assumed that the business will be in existence for a very long period without any intention to close, that is, continue in operation for:
explanation: Going concern: indefinite continued operation unless evidence of imminent close-down.

question_text: According to the course material, dual aspect or double entity concept recognises that for every transaction there are always two parties involved: one party is giving while the other is receiving, and if properly followed assets and liabilities in total must be:
explanation: The technique that reflects this concept is the double entry principle.

question_text: According to the course material, the cost concept states that in recording the value of a company's assets, the value should be stated at cost price or the original cost as this will ensure that all transactions are:
option_a: objectively recorded as against using their current values
explanation: Assets at original cost, not current values, for objectivity.

question_text: According to the course material, according to the accrual concept, revenues should be recognised immediately they are earned while expenses are recognised when they are incurred, but not when the money is:
explanation: Accrual: recognise revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, not on cash.

question_text: According to the course material, the money measurement concept means that for an event to be recorded in the accounting books they must be events that can be measured in terms of money; the records do not show if a company has a good or bad management team, but payment of salaries of N20,000:
option_a: will be recorded in the books of accounts
explanation: Only events measurable in money are recorded.

question_text: According to the course material, the matching concept states that revenues and expenses for any accounting period should be matched with each other so that the profit or loss for the period can be ascertained; this concept brought about adjustments in the final accounts at:
explanation: Matching leads to year-end adjustments.

question_text: According to the course material, the convention of prudence states that profit should not be anticipated when recognising profit to be recorded; figures that will overstate the profit should be disregarded; rather, the profit should be:
explanation: Prudence: do not anticipate profit; rather understate than overstate.

question_text: According to the course material, the convention of materiality requires recognition of items that are material to the company; time should not be wasted in elaborate recording of:
explanation: Whatever will not impair the judgement of a user may not be considered material.

question_text: According to the course material, the convention of consistency requires the adoption and usage of accounting policy and method for a reasonable period; if depreciation is reducing balance, the organisation should follow that method year after year unless a valid change is made and the effect is:
option_a: stated in the final accounts of the year when the change occurs
explanation: Policies should not change arbitrarily; disclose the effect of a valid change.

question_text: According to the course material, shareholders are the owners of a company and they are interested in the performance of the company which includes the profit earned, dividends to be paid and:
explanation: Shareholders care about profit, dividends and net worth, and comparison with similar organisations.

question_text: According to the course material, the government is interested in accounting information to determine the company income tax to be paid, compliance with government rules, and to ensure that the interests of the public are:
explanation: Government: tax, compliance, public interest.

question_text: According to the course material, loan providers are banks and other financial institutions; the liquidity position of the company is of paramount importance to this group to ensure:
option_a: the repayment of their loans as at when due
explanation: Liquidity from accounting information matters to lenders.

question_text: According to the course material, employees use the financial statement to be sure of continuous existence of the organisation which will guarantee their employment, and to compare their remuneration with:
option_a: other comparable companies in the same industry
explanation: Employees want job security and pay comparison.

question_text: According to the course material, accounting information is used by the government to determine the tax payable by companies on their profits, and for individuals such as pay as you earn, and other tax payable such as VAT, all used to formulate:
explanation: Tax figures feed government fiscal policy.

question_text: According to the course material, accounting as a profession in Nigeria has grown with formal educational training by tertiary and professional institutions; accounting requires specialised knowledge involving the combination of:
explanation: A profession requires specialised/formal education; accounting combines theory and practice.

question_text: According to the course material, accounting is a service activity: it does not have physical products that can be bought and sold like manufacturing companies, but it produces information that individuals and organisations can use to:
explanation: Accounting is a service centre providing auxiliary services; the effect cuts across private and government organisations.
